label: diffuse original-phase unit, favors j/0/n/f/r/e/h/u late in long sequences
explanation: Fires sparsely (~1% of steps) almost entirely during the original-input phase (94.5% of mass), with some on the <DEL> step (5%) and essentially never during copying or at t=0. Rate rises with position and L (orig_idx 8 has 12.6x lift; L=9 holds 48% of mass) and with first occurrences of the input token. Input-token preference is graded: j (6.5x), 0, n, f, r, e, h, u. It is also enriched when the sequence starts with v/3/l/d and when m/i/d/p/3 appeared earlier, so it looks like a distributed code over prefix content. No predicate tried reached F1 above 0.31. The recorded predicate (original phase, t>=2, in_tok in {j,0,n,f,r,e,h,u}) covers about 80% of activation mass but has only about 8% precision. Adding first_tok in {v,3,l,d} raises F1 to 0.31 (P 0.27, R 0.34). Restricting to late positions or prefix-set counts did not help.
